propositions: A transient GitHub git-fetch hang during code review times out at 300s, converted to SnapshotFetchError, causing adapter to return BLOCK with review-error, leading to a spurious -1 vote being posted.

The spurious -1 vote removes a change from backfill re-review because reconcile.py pre-filters on has_llm_review_vote and skips already-voted changes, making it permanently unrecoverable without manual intervention.
Infrastructure faults (SnapshotFetchError, TimeoutExpired, TimeoutError, ConnectionError) should result in no vote and no dedup row, allowing backfill to re-pick the change on the next pass.

The fix distinguishes retryable infrastructure faults from review conclusions by adding _is_retryable_infra classifier and returning ABSTAIN decision instead of BLOCK, with voter emitting VOTER_ERROR marker but posting no vote.
An abstained change must remain vote-less so backfill reconciler re-drives it, whereas a genuine blocking finding or non-retryable exception still posts the block value fail-closed as today.
